findings.text: The schema describes subject_scope as 'a PREDICATE over the canonical graph'. Assessments about registry/bank TEXT (all three real instances) are naturally predicates over the RUN LEDGER or the REGISTRY, not the graph. Either the wording admits 'a predicate over a DECLARED population (graph | ledger | registry | manifest)' or such assessments are out of the object's scope -- routed to base; this exercise wrote ledger predicates and said so in-field.

In the pre-attestation regime every row is forced to basis=desired (attestation null) while plane may read APPLIED (the live kuzu compare). basis and plane therefore DIVERGE BY DESIGN: plane says WHERE the evidence was read, basis says HOW STRONG it is admissible as. Not a defect; stated so a consumer does not read basis as the read-plane.

The control is NOT a manifest subject; its interim_status.manifest_ref therefore points at the manifest with an explicit 'not a manifest subject' note. A control that must carry a required manifest_ref shows the field's domain is the manifest, which is correct -- the control lives outside it and says so.

Applied base's 63827 ruling: for the three real bundles s5=METHOD_ACCEPTANCE NOT_ASSESSED is carried as residue and substantive_result is the certificate/decomposition; for the control, s3/s4 ACQUISITION NOT_ASSESSED fire UNKNOWN. The rule discriminates the control from the real runs exactly as intended. The S6 object has no slot for it (additionalProperties:false) -- the PROTO-RECORD carries stage_class; printed beside each instance here.
